metadata.note: The Indianapolis and Vincennes Railroad (chartered 1865) ran 117.8 mi from Indianapolis Union Station south-west via Mooresville, Martinsville, Gosport, Spencer, Freedom, Worthington, Switz City, Bushrod, Sandborn, Edwardsport and Bicknell to Vincennes, plus the 12.3-mile Green County Coal Branch from Bushrod to Dugger. It does NOT run through Bloomfield (Monon / Illinois Central); it crosses the Monon's Bedford - Switz City branch at Switz City. Features are split by operator era (Rule 4): Indianapolis and Vincennes 1868 (Indianapolis - Spencer [ANCHOR]) and 1869-1870 in its own colour; Pennsylvania Company 1871-1904, Vandalia 1905-1916, Pittsburgh, Cincinnati, Chicago & St. Louis 1917-1920, Pennsylvania Railroad 1921-1934 [OPEN], all in PRR colour (the dataset folds PRR Lines West companies into PRR colour). Branch: 1886 [OPEN start]-1904, 1905-1916, 1917-1920, 1921-1923, all PRR colour. Labels follow Rule 6; the Vandalia's PRR-family company string is new ('Vandalia Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad)'), as is 'Pennsylvania Company (Pennsylvania Railroad)'. Freight-only years are not drawn (Rule 1): the main line was freight only by Jan 1952 (later the PC/Conrail Petersburg Secondary and, north of Sandborn, the Indiana Southern Railroad from 1992), and the branch after 1923.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules of 13 Jan 1952), Pennsylvania RR Table 202 INDIANAPOLIS-VINCENNES "Freight Service only" (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt; page image https://archive.org/download/the-official-guide-of-the-railways-images/page/n346.jpg)
not_yet_sourced: Main line end of passenger service: drawn to 1934 [OPEN] (last primary positive, May 1934 Indianapolis Times). Bracket 1934-1951; Wikipedia (citing the 1989 NRHP nomination of the Martinsville depot, not read) says 1940; Feb 1952 Official Guide says freight only. Reading the NRHP nomination (SHAARD, ref 91000268) or a 'last train' newspaper story would settle it.
Whether passenger service ended on the whole main line at once (a Martinsville local may have outlasted through trains) - not known; not split.
Operator 1905-1916: Vandalia (Fowler's 1905 VR timetable) vs PCC&StL (Wikipedia 'Pennsylvania Company' list). Drawn as Vandalia; both are PRR colour.
Operator 1871-1904: Pennsylvania Company per Wikipedia only (secondary); an Official Guide or Poor's Manual of the 1880s-90s would confirm.
Vandalia - PCC&StL merger date: Wikipedia 1 Jan 1917 vs Encyclopedia of Indianapolis 1916; 1917 used.
Opening dates are year-only and secondary (Martinsville July 1868, Spencer 1868 [ANCHOR], Vincennes 1869); the ICC valuation would give exact dates.

Green County Coal Branch: 1886 start is the earliest confirmed year [OPEN], not a known opening; continuity 1886-1923 and the 1923 end rest on Fowler alone; whether service reached Linton proper (vs South Linton) is unclear; the Dugger station site was not located.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Partial opening: the Indianapolis and Vincennes opened Indianapolis - Martinsville about July 1868 (a dealer's catalogue note on an I&V stock certificate - a weak source) and was 'completed to Spencer in 1868' (Counties of Clay and Owen, Indiana, 1884). 1868 is a single anchored year: service certainly ran into 1869 as the line was pushed on to Vincennes (drawn on the full-line feature), but no other year is confirmed for this partial section on its own. Mooresville construction in 1867 (Encyclopedia of Indianapolis) is construction, not proven service, and is not drawn. Do not widen. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (report: 2-3 trains each way daily), not taken from any timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the note cites the 1884 Clay/Owen county history and a stock-certificate catalogue note for the 1868 opening (both secondary; no 1868 timetable seen). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Opened through Indianapolis - Vincennes in 1869 (year only, secondary: Encyclopedia of Indianapolis, 'opened the line to Vincennes in 1869'; Wikipedia Vandalia Railroad, 'completed between its namesake cities in 1869'). Operated by the I&V itself until the Pennsylvania Company took over operation on 1 Apr 1871 (Wikipedia, Pennsylvania Company), so the I&V era is drawn to 1870. Promoted 1865 by Ambrose E. Burnside with IC&L and Pennsylvania backing as part of a route to Cairo that was never completed. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (report: 2-3 trains each way daily), not taken from any timetable.

segments.note: Operated from 1 Apr 1871 by the Pennsylvania Company, the PRR's Lines West operating company (Wikipedia 'Pennsylvania Company' list of operated roads; Wikipedia's Vandalia RR article describes the same event as the PRR 'taking control in 1871'). Ends 31 Dec 1904 at the operator change (consolidation into the Vandalia Railroad), not at an end of service. Coloured PRR as the dataset folds PRR Lines West companies into PRR colour. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (report: 2-3 trains each way daily), not taken from any timetable.

segments.note: The I&V was consolidated into the Vandalia Railroad on 1 Jan 1905. Fowler's legend for line 58 cites a 1905 Vandalia public timetable ('a: 1905(VR)t'), and Centerton is tagged 'ya' - a primary positive for passenger trains in 1905. The Martinsville depot (NRHP 'Martinsville Vandalia Depot', ref 91000268) was built in 1911, indirect evidence of passenger business in this era. OPERATOR CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: Wikipedia's 'Pennsylvania Company' list calls the merged line 'PRR-owned, PCC&St.L operated' from 1 Jan 1905, while Fowler's 1905 Vandalia timetable implies the Vandalia ran its own trains; this feature follows the report in naming the Vandalia. Either way the era takes PRR colour. Ends 31 Dec 1916 at the Vandalia's merger into the PCC&StL (Wikipedia: 1 Jan 1917; the Encyclopedia of Indianapolis says 1916 - also a recorded conflict). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (report: 2-3 trains each way daily), not taken from any timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the note cites Fowler's 1905 Vandalia timetable letter (start) and the 1911 Martinsville depot (indirect); the 1916 end is a corporate date from Wikipedia. Service in 1906-1916 is not sourced year by year; headway not sourced.

segments.note: [OPEN] The PRR leased the PCC&StL from 1 Jan 1921 and ran this as its Vincennes Branch ('V&I Branch'). Passenger service is confirmed to 1934 by the Indianapolis Times: a 6 May 1934 excursion special Indianapolis - Vincennes 'Via Pennsylvania Railroad' (1 May 1934, p.3), and the 4-5 May 1934 Lilly extortion-plot reports of detectives taking a regular train from Martinsville toward Vincennes on 1 May 1934 and alighting near Paragon (p.1). 1934 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end. The end lies somewhere in 1934-1951: Wikipedia ('Martinsville station', citing the 1989 NRHP nomination, not read directly) says passenger service ended in 1940, and the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 202 shows the line as 'Freight Service only'. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued after passengers ended; the line south of Sandborn was later abandoned and the north end survives as the Indiana Southern Railroad. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (report: 1-2 trains each way daily in the 1930s), not from any timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the note cites the May 1934 Indianapolis Times items (last primary positive), the Feb 1952 Official Guide (first primary negative) and Wikipedia's secondary 1940 end. Start is the 1921 lease date. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: [OPEN start] 1886 is the earliest CONFIRMED year (Appletons' Guide 1886, per Fowler), not a known opening date; the nature of the 1886 service (local or mixed) is not known. Continuity 1886-1904 is not sourced. Ends 31 Dec 1904 at the operator change to the Vandalia. Branch from Bushrod (main-line mp 85.1) via Island City and South Linton to Dugger, 12.3 mi (Fowler IN line 59), built for the Greene County coal field developed from 1884. Fowler's line header reads 'passenger service 1886AG, miners trains until 1923'. Miners' (workmen's) trains carried passengers and count as passenger service under Rule 1. 'Green County' is Fowler's spelling. headway_min is an ESTIMATE; no timetable seen.
sources: Segment-level: the note cites Fowler IN line 59 ('passenger service 1886AG') for the 1886 start; the 1904 end is a corporate date. Continuity 1886-1904 and headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Bushrod - Dugger: traced 11.6 mi against a documented 12.3 mi (Fowler IN line 59). No straight-line legs; all on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=PRR (0 mi on the Illinois Central / INRD, Monon or Milwaukee Road grades in the same coal field). Distance from each documented place to the drawn line: Bushrod 0.03 km, Island City 0.26, Linton (town point) 1.26, Dugger (town point) 1.49 km. The PRR branch ran south of both town centres (Fowler lists a 'South Linton' station); the Dugger station site was not located, and the drawn line stops at the PRR line's closest approach to Dugger, which may account for most of the 0.7 mi shortfall. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the grade as OSM maps it at abandonment, a later state than 1886-1923; mine spurs and any re-alignment are not represented.
